package_info.package_versions: Unknown (compromised versions prior to public disclosure in March 2024)
package_info.why_malicious: The Tornado Cash user interface was compromised by a malicious developer who injected JavaScript code that exfiltrated users’ private deposit notes to an unauthorized external server. This enabled the attacker to steal funds from users by obtaining the cryptographic secrets required to withdraw assets from the platform.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user interacts with the Tornado Cash web UI to generate or handle a deposit note
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript code within the Tornado Cash web UI repository (exact file path not specified in report)
required_permissions: Network access (ability to make outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests)
Access to in-browser memory (read/write access to deposit notes and cryptographic secrets)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user interacts with the web UI to generate or handle a deposit note, the code accesses the user's private deposit note from in-browser memory, then sends its value to an attacker-controlled external server via HTTPS POST, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive cryptographic credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive cryptographic material (the deposit note) and transmits it to an external, unauthorized server. This is a direct violation of user privacy and security, as the deposit note is the only secret required to withdraw funds from Tornado Cash.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Tornado Cash UI should never transmit private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets to any external server. All cryptographic operations and secret handling are expected to remain strictly local to the user's browser environment.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry code may send non-sensitive usage statistics or error logs to external servers, but should never transmit private cryptographic secrets such as deposit notes. Any code sending such secrets externally is highly anomalous.
key_indicators: JavaScript code accessing in-browser cryptographic secrets (e.g., deposit notes)
Outbound network requests (fetch/XHR) to domains not affiliated with tornado.cash
Transmission of deposit notes or wallet secrets in the body of HTTP(S) POST requests
Presence of code referencing deposit notes in conjunction with network exfiltration logic

attack_chain.action: A malicious developer commits JavaScript code to the Tornado Cash UI repository that is designed to exfiltrate user deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious code is deployed to the production web interface, making it accessible to all users.

attack_chain.action: A user interacts with the compromised Tornado Cash UI and generates or handles a private deposit note during normal use.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious code executes in the user's browser session.

attack_chain.action: The malicious code captures the user's private deposit note from browser memory and sends it to the attacker's external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker receives the stolen deposit notes, enabling unauthorized access to user funds.

attack_chain.action: The attacker uses the stolen deposit notes to withdraw funds from Tornado Cash, draining affected user accounts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of user funds from the platform.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in DeFi UIs accessing and exfiltrating private cryptographic material such as deposit notes
Network requests initiated by the UI to non-official, non-tornado.cash domains during sensitive operations (e.g., deposit or withdrawal workflows)
Transmission of deposit notes or wallet secrets via HTTP(S) POST requests from the browser
file_indicators: New or modified JavaScript files in the UI codebase containing fetch or XMLHttpRequest calls to unknown or untrusted domains
Inline scripts or obfuscated code blocks that reference deposit notes, secrets, or cryptographic material in conjunction with network communication logic
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from the Tornado Cash UI to domains not associated with tornado.cash (e.g., attacker-server.com)
Unusual network traffic patterns originating from the UI during deposit or withdrawal operations, especially to previously unseen domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform static and dynamic analysis of DeFi web application codebases to identify JavaScript that accesses private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets and initiates network requests to external servers. Monitor network traffic from the UI for POST requests to non-official domains, particularly during deposit or withdrawal workflows. Flag any code that combines access to cryptographic secrets with outbound network communication to untrusted endpoints.
